name: Electric Assisted Bicycle
description: A bicycle with pedals and an electric motor, in one of three classes: Class 1 pedal assist to 20 mph, Class 2 throttle to 20 mph, and Class 3 pedal assist to 28 mph. Defined by Oregon Revised Statutes §801.258 as rewritten by HB 4103 (2024), which replaced the old 1,000-watt, 20 mph definition, and treated as a bicycle by §814.405.
restrictions: Must be equipped with pedals; the statute sets no motor wattage limit since HB 4103 (2024) dropped the former 1,000-watt cap
Class 1 assists only while the rider pedals and stops assisting at 20 mph
Class 2 can be propelled by its motor without pedaling and stops assisting at 20 mph
Class 3 assists only while the rider pedals, stops assisting at 28 mph, and must have a speedometer
Riders of any class must be 16 or older
From January 1, 2027 (HB 4007, 2026), riders must be 14 or older for Class 1 and 16 or older for Class 2 and Class 3, and riders of any age in a bicycle safety program may ride Class 1 or Class 2
Riders and passengers under 16 must wear an approved bicycle helmet; a parent, or a rider carrying such a passenger, is liable for the violation
No driver's license needed for a rider who meets the age limit
Treated as a bicycle, not a motor vehicle: no title, registration or insurance
May not be ridden on a sidewalk
Allowed in bicycle lanes and on bicycle paths like any bicycle
In Oregon state parks, allowed on trails open to bicycles and on wet sand on the ocean shore unless posted otherwise; kept off dry sand and dunes

From January 1, 2027, selling a vehicle as an electric assisted bicycle, or as a given class, when it doesn't fit the definition or is built to be switched, modified or app-unlocked out of it is a traffic violation and an unlawful trade practice
From January 1, 2027, a new e-bike or its battery or charger may only be sold with a certification mark from an accredited testing laboratory
